# 1 Clement Chapter 43 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 43 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_043_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 43

**43:1** And what wonder is it if those who were entrusted with such a great work in Christ sent forward men of this character, when even the blessed Moses, "a faithful servant in all his house," recorded in the sacred books all the injunctions given to him?

**43:2** And after him the other prophets also followed, bearing witness to the legislation he gave.

**43:3** For when rivalry arose concerning the priesthood, and the tribes were contending among themselves about which of them should be adorned with the glorious name, he commanded the twelve tribal leaders to bring to him rods inscribed with the name of each tribe; and taking them, he bound and sealed them with the rings of the tribal leaders, and placed them in the tent of witness on the table of God.

**43:4** And shutting the tent, he sealed the keys in the same way as well as the rods.

**43:5** And he said: "Brothers, the tribe whose rod blossoms — this God has chosen to be priests and to minister to him."

**43:6** And when early morning came, he called together all Israel, that is, the six hundred thousand men, and showed the seals to the tribal leaders, and opened the tent of witness and drew out the rods; and the rod of Aaron was found not only to have blossomed, but also to be bearing fruit.

**43:7** What do you think, beloved? Did not Moses know beforehand that this would happen? He certainly knew. But in order that there should be no disorder in Israel, he acted in this way, so that the name of the true and only God might be glorified — to whom be the glory for ever and ever. Amen.

---

*EMET renders with maximal literalness. The Numbers 17 narrative of Aaron's blossoming rod is retold as an argument that orderly, divinely-validated appointment of priestly leadership is the ancient biblical pattern. Clement uses this typologically: just as Moses dealt with priestly rivalry through an orderly divine sign, so the apostles (by analogy) established orderly appointment of bishops.*
